description: Experience the ultimate comfort food with a Classic BLT Sandwich, a timeless American favorite. This simple yet satisfying recipe highlights the perfect trifecta of crispy bacon, crisp lettuce, and juicy ripe tomatoes. Enjoy a quick and delicious lunch that never disappoints.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bacon
instructions.text: Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Drain excess fat and place bacon on a plate lined with paper towels to cool and crisp further.

instructions.title: Toast the Bread
instructions.text: While the bacon cools, toast the bread slices in a toaster or a hot skillet until golden brown and crisp to your desired preference.

instructions.title: Slice Vegetables
instructions.text: Wash and thoroughly dry the lettuce leaves. Slice the ripe tomatoes into even, moderately thick rounds. Season the tomato slices lightly with salt and pepper.

instructions.title: Assemble the Base
instructions.text: Spread a generous and even layer of good quality mayonnaise on one side of each toasted bread slice. Ensure full coverage for maximum flavor.

instructions.title: Layer the Ingredients
instructions.text: On four of the mayo-coated toast slices, arrange a layer of lettuce leaves, followed by the seasoned tomato slices. Distribute evenly.

instructions.title: Add Crispy Bacon
instructions.text: Place three slices of the crispy bacon over the tomatoes on each of the four sandwich bases. Break bacon slices in half if needed to fit neatly.

instructions.title: Complete the Sandwich
instructions.text: Top each assembled base with the remaining four slices of mayo-coated toast. Gently press down on each sandwich. For ease of eating, cut each sandwich in half diagonally and serve immediately.

tips: For perfectly crispy bacon, start with a cold pan and cook slowly over medium-low heat, flipping often to render fat evenly.
Always use ripe, in-season tomatoes for the best flavor and juiciness; they are the heart of a truly great BLT.
Serve your BLT immediately after assembly to prevent the toast from getting soggy, ensuring every bite is perfectly crisp and fresh.
